# Packaging and deployment

## Offline source and static builds

The delivered source is usable without npm installation because import maps and
a Node loader point to the checked-in workspace and genuine vendored browser/
Node distributions. `npm run build` regenerates 75 direct XAML modules and copies
runtime assets to `dist/`. It intentionally excludes font files.

`dist/` is a complete static application. It uses relative asset paths and needs
an HTTP server with correct JavaScript/WASM MIME types. Deploy the complete tree,
not just index.html or app.js. The archive contains a substantial native WASM
renderer; it is not an empty CDN loader.

## npm tarballs

```sh
npm run pack:all
```

Each of the 18 packages is packed independently with source, README, LICENSE and
NOTICE. Exact internal version dependencies are recorded in package.json;
ReactiveWeb, RxJS and SkiaSharpWeb dependencies use the inspected versions.
`artifacts/npm/manifest.json` records file sizes and SHA-256 hashes.

These new scoped packages are not published. Installing a single tarball cannot
resolve unpublished sibling dependencies from a public registry. Install all
local siblings together (and the external dependency versions), or publish the
entire dependency graph first. The provided import-map/loader path avoids this
registry requirement for development. No npm publication/token operation is
performed by the packaging script or workflow.

The tarballs do not embed the complete offline vendor directory. Standard npm
consumers obtain external dependencies through their dependency manifests and
must copy the Skia native assets according to that dependency's packaging guide.
The standalone catalog archive, by contrast, does include the vendor assets.

The actual local package-consumer check extracts every tarball into a fresh
node_modules and resolves sibling packages through Node's ESM resolver. Only the
external vendored dependencies are mapped by its test loader. This tests packed
files and imports, not public-registry installation or every bundler.

There is no generated TypeScript declaration surface or CommonJS build in this
alpha. Package/module dependency cycles associated with browser/reactive
integration are lazy at startup, and eager initialization should not be added
to those cycle edges without tests.

## GitHub workflows

The supplied CI builds, runs the recorded Node suite, packs, checks ordinary HTTP browser deployment, and runs the RGBA and two-DPI scrollbar suites. This workflow was not executed remotely in this continuation.
The Pages workflow is manual (`workflow_dispatch`) and deploys dist after its
build. Enable Pages/GitHub Actions in the destination repository before invoking
it. No destination repository was supplied for this delivery, and no commit,
push, registry publication or Pages deployment has been performed.

The scripts/CI definitions are supplied source; only the local test reports
establish executed results. Review action permissions and pin action commit
hashes according to your organization's policy before production deployment.

## Upstream text helper dependency (0.4 continuation)

The source ZIP remains offline runnable. The independent Skia npm tarball now
references the exact SkiaSharpWeb Git commit in `docs/upstream-lock.json`, because
published npm 0.5.0 lacks the new browser-text subpath. Do not replace that pin with
0.5.0. Update it to a versioned registry release only after verifying its export
and runtime hashes. The tarball consumer verification resolves bundled dependencies;
it is not a public npm/Git install test.

## Current release integrity

The 0.5 continuation preserves the original 0.4 archive and all 991 baseline
manifest hashes. `npm run verify:release` requires completed tests/build/consumer
reports with one exact runtime/source fingerprint. `archive.py` then writes a
per-file SHA-256 source manifest, scans source and nested packages for font files,
and creates source, static and npm archives. A separate clean extraction validates
all final ZIP hashes and reruns tests/build/consumer checks; see the delivered
extraction report. No remote repository writes or package publication occurred.

## Worker graph

`avalonia-browser` includes `worker-assets/`, generated by `build-workers.mjs`.
Its manifest binds all graph bytes and the sample application graph to the source
fingerprint. The native WASM remains in the existing vendor assets and must be
served at the explicit runtime URL. The source/static ZIPs contain these assets.
Other applications can use their own bundled worker application module; see
THREADING.md for a complete factory and explicit relative-import example.

The 18 npm tarballs are not published by this delivery. The offline consumer
extracts actual tarballs and checks exported protocol functions and worker entry
files in addition to the previous binding/XAML/control tests. No font binaries are
bundled, including nested tarballs.
